# Coffee Shop Challenge

```{r}
##libraries
library(mapview)
library(tidycensus)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(osmdata)
library(tigris)
library(dplyr)
```

#### Shop: "Thistle and Kona." 

My coffee shop will offer the Leeward side of Oahu a taste of a culture on the other side of the world, the UK, and mostly Scotland, and combine it with already loved local flavors. From experience and what I see on social media, Sottish, Irish, and English cultures are romanticized, mysticized, and often depicted in fairytale-esque light. Because of this, and the lack of competition for this combination of flavors combined with increased popularity in coffee shops, I believe this venture could succeed. I will use my geo computational skills then, to see if the physical shop could succeed as well, if competition, property, location, etc are taken into account.

### Step 1 - Logo

Every good business needs a name and nice logo, create one manually or with AI for your new cafe and save it as a .png that will show up in your rendered .qmd .html file. (***2 points***)

!["Thistle & Kona" logo](images/logo.png){width="50%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="Mug with tartan pattern"}

### Step 2 - Finding a location

Location: **Halekuai Center at Kapolei,** 563-565 Farrington Hwy, Kapolei, HI 96707

Lat/long: 21.33848629424707, -158.07787057835054

Reason for location: Leeward coast potentially has less coffee-shop competition and cheaper square footage compared to town.

Mapped:

```{r}
pt <- st_sf(name = "Halekuai Center", geometry = st_sfc(st_point(c(-158.07787057835054, 21.33848629424707)), crs = 4326))

mapview(pt)
```

### Step 3 - Map the competition

```{r}
##getting coffee shops on oahu data fram
oahu_bb <- c(xmin = -158.30, ymin = 21.24, xmax = -157.63, ymax = 21.73)

cafe_query <- opq(bbox = oahu_bb, timeout = 180) |> add_osm_features(features = list("amenity" = "cafe", "shop" = "coffee"))

osm_raw <- osmdata_sf(cafe_query)

cafe_points <- as.data.frame(osm_raw$osm_points)

```

```{r}
##filtering dataframe to just kapolei geometries and maping
coords <- st_coordinates(cafe_points$geometry) 

cafe_west <- cafe_points |>
  mutate(lon = coords[, 1], lat = coords[, 2]) |>
  mutate(area = case_when(
    lon > -158.25 & lon < -158.12 & lat > 21.38 & lat < 21.52 ~ "Waianae",
    lon > -158.12 & lon < -158.04 & lat > 21.29 & lat < 21.41 ~ "Kapolei",
    lon > -158.04 & lon < -157.95 & lat > 21.29 & lat < 21.35 ~ "Ewa",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(area))
```

```{r}
##mapping fltered points using mapviw
mapview(st_as_sf(cafe_west), zcol = "name")
```

There doesn't seem to be tough competition, there are a few Starbucks locations and a few Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf locations, though. I will note that a few cafes did not make it to this list, such as Island Vintage in Kapolei, only about a mile away from my location.

A few locations popped up that are not explicitly coffee shops too, like Countryside Cafe and Mountain Magic Shave ice.

I included the Waianae range in my map of competition because I know majority of workers in Waianae commute to town or Kapolei regularly, so I did not want to neglect those locations.

In all, there are only 10 unique locations spanning majority of the leeward coast, limiting my competition, and only 7 locations competing in Kapolei.

### Step 4.1 - Resident Customer Demographics

How can we map some spatial information describing your potential customers. Use `tidycensus` to pull in some census data for the tract your coffee shop is in.

Within the get_acs() function think of putting in some of these variable codes based on what is most relevant to your coffee shop (***4 points***)

| Code | Name in script | What it measures | Universe (denominator) |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| B01001_001 | `total_pop` | Total population | All residents |
| B01001_007 | `m_18_19` | Male, 18–19 years | All residents |
| B01001_008 | `m_20` | Male, 20 years | All residents |
| B01001_009 | `m_21` | Male, 21 years | All residents |
| B01001_010 | `m_22_24` | Male, 22–24 years | All residents |
| B01001_011 | `m_25_29` | Male, 25–29 years | All residents |
| B01001_012 | `m_30_34` | Male, 30–34 years | All residents |
| B01001_031 | `f_18_19` | Female, 18–19 years | All residents |
| B01001_032 | `f_20` | Female, 20 years | All residents |
| B01001_033 | `f_21` | Female, 21 years | All residents |
| B01001_034 | `f_22_24` | Female, 22–24 years | All residents |
| B01001_035 | `f_25_29` | Female, 25–29 years | All residents |
| B01001_036 | `f_30_34` | Female, 30–34 years | All residents |
| B19013_001 | `med_hh_income` | Median household income (inflation-adjusted dollars) | Households |
| B08301_001 | `commuters` | Total workers 16+ (base for commute shares) | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_010 | `transit` | Commute by public transportation (excl. taxi) | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_018 | `bike` | Commute by bicycle | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_019 | `walk` | Walked to work | Workers 16+ |
| B08301_021 | `wfh` | Worked from home | Workers 16+ |
| B14001_001 | `school_pop` | Population 3+ (base for enrollment) | Population 3+ |
| B14001_008 | `college_ug` | Enrolled in college, undergraduate | Population 3+ |
| B14001_009 | `college_grad` | Enrolled in graduate or professional school | Population 3+ |
| B15003_001 | `pop_25plus` | Population 25+ (base for education) | Population 25+ |
| B15003_022 | `bachelors` | Bachelor’s degree | Population 25+ |
| B15003_023 | `masters` | Master’s degree | Population 25+ |
| B15003_024 | `professional` | Professional school degree (JD, MD, etc.) | Population 25+ |
| B15003_025 | `doctorate` | Doctorate degree | Population 25+ |
| B25064_001 | `med_gross_rent` | Median gross rent (residential, rent + utilities) | Renter-occupied units paying cash rent |

```{r}
vars <- c(
  total_pop   = "B01003_001",  # total population
  commuters   = "B08301_001",  # workers 16+ 
  transit     = "B08301_010",  # workers commuting by public transportation
  median_rent = "B25064_001",  # median gross rent
  male        = "B01001_002",  # male population
  female      = "B01001_026"   # female population
)

tracts <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = vars,
  state     = "HI",
  county    = "Honolulu",
  year      = 2023,
  survey    = "acs5",
  geometry  = TRUE,
  output    = "wide"
)

tracts_clean <- tracts |>
  transmute(
    GEOID, NAME,
    total_pop   = total_popE,
    commuters   = commutersE,
    transit     = transitE,
    median_rent = median_rentE,
    male        = maleE,
    female      = femaleE,
    pct_transit = transit / commuters,
    pct_female  = female / total_pop
  )
```

I have my different variables cleaned and ready to view that I may be interested in. I chose total population, commuters, transit, median rent, and male and female variables, since these may give me a glimpse into the amount of people in my stores chosen location, how many commute, what the rent in the area may be as a gauge for income (?) and female vs male. Now I can map each easily using mapview.

```{r}
mapview(tracts_clean, zcol = "total_pop")
```

```{r}
mapview(tracts_clean, zcol = "pct_female")
```

```{r}
mapview(tracts_clean, zcol = "median_rent")
```

```{r}
mapview(tracts_clean, zcol = "commuters")
```

Take aways:

Population: Moderate population size, similar to other tracts on the island excluding outliers.

pct_female: Evenly split similar to other tracts on island, not much change dependent on location.

Relatively higher rent than other areas of Oahu, which could signify a increase in

### Step 4.2 - Working Customer Demographics

### Step 5 - What's nearby?

Utilizing [isochrones](https://walker-data.com/posts/accessibility-surface/) show us whats a 5 minute drive and 10 minute walk from your shop. Think about utilizing rush hour traffic data when people would grab a coffee before work (if that is your audience/customer base) (***4 points)***

At the county level, use the [eagle i dataset](https://www.osti.gov/biblio/3012826) to show how many times the county your coffee shop is in lost power in 2025. Make a line plot of outages over time with `ggplot` (***3 points***)
